content: Disease transmission refers to the process by which an infectious disease or pathogen is transferred or communicated from one individual to another within a population of humans or groups of other animals. There are two primary modes of disease transmission: 1. Horizontal disease transmission occurs when a disease is passed between individuals of the same generation, such as peers within the same age group. This type of transmission can happen through: Direct contact, which includes actions like licking, touching, or biting. Indirect contact, which involves the use of vectors (organisms like mosquitoes or ticks that carry pathogens) or fomites (inanimate objects like doorknobs or utensils that facilitate disease spread without direct physical contact). 2. Vertical disease transmission involves the transfer of a disease-causing agent from parent to offspring. This typically occurs when the mother transmits the disease to her child through bodily fluids, and in some cases, through breast milk.
